purpose: Compare the effect of the initial tip-synapse resistance on synchronization and later parameter normalization in the archived PHASE6 case.

condition.source_match_note: The seven relevant current local C++ source files were compared to the server working tree after LF normalization and matched. The same Release Console binary was used for both runs.

input_pair.input_comparison: Interface.xml and Project.ini are byte-identical. In both Model_00.xml and Parameters_00.xml, the coordinated cold-start resistance fields change from 86 MOhm to 20 MOhm: SynapseResistanceBase, the four-value TipSynapseResistance vector, and the four Dendrite{1..4}_1 ExcSynapse1 Resistance values. The fixed gamma is the same in both; AutoEstimateAttenuationGamma=0 was inserted/set in both because the archived base omitted that tag. Runtime reset audit confirmed the intended Rs in each arm.

86M.main_training: reached Need=0 and phase Done after PostTune; PostTune landscape_ok=false.

20M.main_training: C++ refused before PostTune: unresolved amplitude overshoot at ResistanceMax, dendrite 2, tip_R=Rmax=10 GOhm, amp_dt=-0.000525748, length=49, W3=0; Need=1.
20M.classification_quality: not evaluated; C++ training did not converge

interpretation: For this exact PHASE6 / PSI-on / fixed-gamma condition, lowering initial Rs to 20 MOhm did not change the first observed synchronization gate: both runs passed it on iteration 35 at about 71.924 s.

The lower initial Rs raised the reference amplitude by about 4.44 times. Subsequent parameter normalization therefore targeted a much higher amplitude and later refused at Rmax. This supports preserving the historical 86 MOhm cold-start for this configuration; it does not establish a universal result across patterns, PSI modes, or trainers.

This pair does not show that Rs has no effect on synchronization dynamics; it shows only that the first synchronization gate was reached at the same iteration/time in this pair. The trajectories and final Rs differ.
The 86 MOhm run's landscape_ok=false is a quality/post-train outcome distinct from Need=0 convergence. No Test classification was run for either arm.

Both wrapper exit files report rc=143 because the process was signaled after the terminal trainer result was recorded. The trainer outcome comes from the C++ log and saved state, not the wrapper exit code.
